hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Guinea-Bissau and Mauritania || generally low, rolling, plains rising to foothills in southeast || westernmost country on the African continent; The Gambia is almost an enclave within Senegal || Resources: fish, phosphates, iron ore || Exports: gold, refined petroleum, phosphoric acid, fish, cement (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: generally low, rolling, plains rising to foothills in southeast || Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Guinea-Bissau and Mauritania

climate.excerpt: tropical; hot, humid; rainy season (May to November) has strong southeast winds; dry season (December to April) dominated by hot, dry, harmattan wind || lowlands seasonally flooded; periodic droughts

economy.excerpt: lower middle-income, services-driven West African economy; key mining, construction, agriculture, and fishing industries; tourism and exports hit hard by COVID-19; large informal economy; developing offshore oil and gas fields; systemic corruption || Exports: gold, refined petroleum, phosphoric acid, fish, cement (2023) || Industries: agricultural and fish processing, phosphate mining, fertilizer production, petroleum refining, zircon, and gold mining, construction materials, ship construction and repair

peopleAndCulture.from: People and Society > Languages, Religions, Ethnic groups, Urbanization
peopleAndCulture.excerpt: French (official), Wolof, Pulaar, Jola, Mandinka, Serer, Soninke || Muslim 97.2% (most adhere to one of the four main Sufi brotherhoods), Christian 2.7% (mostly Roman Catholic) (2019 est.) || Wolof 39.7%, Pulaar 27.5%, Sereer 16%, Mandinka 4.9%, Jola 4.2%, Soninke 2.4%, other 5.4% (includes Europeans and persons of Lebanese descent) (2019 est.)
